market_brief: The weekend tally shows how violent the AI unwind was: the S&P 500 (-8.6% w/w to 6,910) fell for a seventh straight session, its longest losing streak since February 2020; the Nasdaq 100 lost 10.4%, the SOX 17.1% and the VIX nearly doubled to 35.9. Nvidia had its worst week since 2008 (-23%) and slipped below Alphabet in market value as an SEC accounting probe reportedly zeroes in on geographic revenue reporting. Havens and deleveraging dominated cross-asset moves: the 10Y fell 24bp on the week to 4.91% even with a December Fed hike ~89-97% priced, DXY was steady near 103.8, gold fell 9.5% to ~$3,515, silver 16%, and bitcoin kept sliding on Saturday to below $56k (lowest since September 2024), under the $58.1k in this morning's snapshot. India remained the counter-trend: Nifty +2.6% and Nifty Bank +5.9% on the week to a record, with FIIs buying every session (~₹32,600 cr) and the rupee at a seven-month high (~92.67), though an expected RBI hike on Dec 4 and a holiday-shortened week with US PCE are next.
ai_brief: The capital-markets story still leads AI: Nvidia's SEC probe and record weekly drop, plus reported talks to buy diffusion-LLM startup Inception, while private marks keep rising (Databricks reportedly at ~$225B, Genesis AI $500M at $3.5B) and Palo Alto paid $4.5B for Applied Compute. On research, the Claude-assisted Riemann claim now comes with a companion Navier-Stokes proof and early expert sentiment that the Lean formalization holds, though peer review is pending. Signal began blocking OS-level AI assistants from reading its screen, Apple released Depth Pro 2 weights, and newsletters are debating circular AI financing and whether the bubble has popped.

items.headline: Update: Nvidia books worst week since 2008 and slips below Alphabet in market value
items.summary: Nvidia closed Friday at $125.53, down about 23% on the week, wiping roughly $1T off its value; LSEG data put it around $3.4T versus Alphabet's ~$3.44T. Coverage says the reported SEC accounting probe may center on how Nvidia reports revenue by geography; the company has not commented on the focus.

items.headline: S&P 500's seven-day losing run is its longest since February 2020; VIX jumps to 35.9
items.summary: The Nasdaq closed at 22,617.73, below its 2025 year-end level, and the VIX rose 26% on the day. Anthropic ended at $88.91 after its $83 IPO, and JPMorgan is cited as expecting three Fed hikes.

items.headline: Update: Bitcoin crashes below $56,000, lowest since September 2024
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped nearly 10% to about $55,800 early Saturday as roughly $2.4B of crypto derivatives positions were liquidated in 24 hours. The slide extends Friday's risk-off move and leaves BTC down about a quarter in November.

items.headline: Waller's 'shock' remarks lift odds of a half-point December Fed hike to 10%
items.summary: After Governor Waller again floated a 50bp move, CME FedWatch odds of a half-point hike at the Dec 8-9 meeting rose to 10% from about 3%, with a quarter-point hike seen as the base case. Friday's haven rally nonetheless pulled the 10Y yield down 24bp on the week to 4.91%.

items.headline: PBoC holds loan prime rates for an 18th month; polls lean toward a BoJ hike to 1.5% in December
items.summary: China kept the 1-year LPR at 3.0% and 5-year at 3.5% as expected. A Reuters poll had 86% of economists expecting the Bank of Japan to raise rates to 1.50% at its Dec 17-18 meeting, with October core CPI seen picking up to 2.3%.

items.headline: Nifty gains 2.6% for a fourth winning week; Bank Nifty +5.9% to a record as FIIs buy every session
items.summary: PSU Bank (+6.7%) and Private Bank (+5.7%) indices led while Metal and IT lagged; FIIs bought a net ~₹32,647 cr in cash for the week as DIIs sold ~₹12,698 cr. Nifty is about 2% below its January record close and up nearly 12% in November.

items.headline: RBI seen hiking repo 25bp to 5.75% on Dec 4 after October CPI of 6.09%
items.summary: A quarter-point increase at the Dec 2-4 policy meeting is widely expected, per weekly market roundups. The rupee firmed about 0.8% on the week to a seven-month high on foreign inflows, which may ease imported-inflation pressure.

items.headline: SEBI caps unhedged rupee-derivative positions at $5M, weighs tying margin-trading limits to free float
items.summary: The regulator is also aiming to cut FPI onboarding time to five days, according to the weekly roundup. The measures land as November heads for record foreign portfolio inflows into Indian equities.

items.headline: Max Healthcare jumps 14% on Macquarie upgrade; Tata Motors PV falls 7% on soft JLR margin guide
items.summary: Max Healthcare led Nifty weekly gainers after the upgrade, and Maruti rose 9% as metal costs eased. Tata Motors PV lagged after JLR guided its FY27 EBIT margin to 2-3%.

items.headline: Mahanadi Coalfields' ₹8,981 crore IPO, a full offer for sale, closes Monday
items.summary: The Coal India unit's issue closes on Nov 23 with listing slated for Nov 27. It is one of the largest PSU offerings of the year.

items.headline: Micron loses 23.6% in a week as TrendForce flags flat-to-lower NAND contract prices
items.summary: MU closed Friday at $594.51, down nearly 14% on the day on heavy volume. TrendForce warned on Nov 19 that NAND contract prices could be flat to down up to 5% in Q1 2027, adding a cyclical worry to the AI selloff.

items.headline: Nvidia reportedly nears deal to buy diffusion-model startup Inception for over $500M
items.summary: The Information reported that Nvidia is close to acquiring Inception, which builds diffusion-based language models. Neither company has confirmed the talks.

items.headline: Week's chip pressure points: short report on AMD and reported Google TPU order cut at Broadcom
items.summary: A short seller alleged possible export-rule violations involving China at AMD, sending it below its 200-day average, and reports said Google trimmed Broadcom TPU orders by about 20%. Palo Alto's beat-and-raise lifted cybersecurity peers against the tide.

items.headline: Fintwit focus: Huang-return petition, Nvidia's 8x forward P/E and 'circular financing' critiques
items.summary: A petition to reinstate Jensen Huang passed 180,000 signatures though Nvidia's board reportedly isn't considering it; bulls point to a ~8x forward multiple under interim CEO Kress. Ed Zitron's CNBC critique of circular Nvidia-Oracle-lab financing circulated widely, while Oracle says its OpenAI contract is fully funded after a $20B raise.

items.headline: Weekly: gold -9% to lowest since September 2025, silver -16%, Brent -6%
items.summary: Gold futures ended near $3,539, about a third below January's record, as margin-driven selling hit precious metals. Brent fell about 6% on the week to ~$89.9 despite Iranian claims of tankers striking mines near Hormuz earlier in the week.

items.headline: Week ahead: flash PMIs Mon, India shut Tue, US GDP and PCE Wed, Thanksgiving Thu, early close Fri
items.summary: Dell reports Tuesday; Wednesday's October PCE is the last major inflation print before the Dec 8-9 FOMC. India's Q2 FY27 GDP is due Nov 30, MSCI changes take effect Dec 1 and the RBI decides on Dec 4.

items.headline: Update: Riemann claim gains a companion Navier-Stokes proof; experts lean toward the Lean code holding
items.summary: Mathematicians quoted by TechCrunch largely expect Levent Alpöge's Lean-formalized result to check out, though the human-readable argument isn't yet understood. Alpöge and Tristan Buckmaster also released a related Navier-Stokes proof, while a rival all-human GRH draft by Alessandro Masullo awaits review.

items.headline: Palo Alto Networks to buy Applied Compute for $4.5B in stock
items.summary: The 2025-founded startup, started by ex-OpenAI researchers, helps enterprises train and deploy open-weight models; co-founder Yash Patil becomes co-chief AI officer. Palo Alto paired the deal with 39% fiscal Q1 revenue growth and raised guidance.

items.headline: Private marks keep climbing: Databricks reportedly eyes ~$225B; Genesis AI raises $500M at $3.5B
items.summary: Databricks is reportedly in early talks to raise several billion dollars at about $225B, up from $190B in August. Robotics startup Genesis AI closed a $500M Series A, and Elon Musk said Optimus could do dishes within 12-18 months.

items.headline: Signal starts blocking OS-level AI assistants from reading chats on iOS and Android
items.summary: Signal now blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and switches on Android's Screen Security when an assistant tries to read the screen; it says macOS can't be protected the same way. It asked Apple, Google and Microsoft for a developer opt-out from OS AI agents.

items.headline: Apple releases Depth Pro 2 weights for metric depth from photos and video
items.summary: The model family spans 24M to 872M parameters and estimates per-pixel metric depth from a single image, video or live feed. Weights are on Hugging Face under a research-only, non-commercial license.

items.headline: Architect Labs unveils 'Frostbite', a CPU it says AI agents designed end to end
items.summary: The startup says its AI systems produced the instruction set, RTL and verification for a 7nm design, claiming a 4.59x perf-per-watt edge across 25 workloads. Results are self-reported and pre-silicon.

items.headline: Trending: OpenSRE CI-failure agent, phone-harness and agent-skills frameworks
items.summary: Tracer-Cloud's Apache-licensed OpenSRE, a CLI agent that triages failed CI runs and proposes fixes, climbed past 12k stars. Repos letting coding agents drive real phones and skill bundles such as obra/superpowers also trended, per daily digests.

items.headline: Google workers petition for schools to get Search without AI features
items.summary: More than 540 employees reportedly signed a petition asking that schools be able to disable Gemini-powered features in Search. The request was made public on Nov 19.

items.headline: Update: DeepSeek's ~100B yuan round registered; new investors hold about 17.3%
items.summary: Caixin reports the second external round closed with business-registration changes on Nov 17, ahead of a planned STAR Market listing. The first round in July raised 50B yuan at a 350B yuan post-money valuation.

items.headline: Newsletter focus: Nvidia's probe and CEO search, circular AI financing, and Chollet on ARC progress
items.summary: Weekend newsletters are weighing whether the selloff marks a bubble top, with attention on Nvidia's SEC probe and leadership, Oracle's funding, and reported stranded H200 inventory in Hong Kong. François Chollet's point that frontier models went from ~5% to near-human on ARC-1 since mid-2024 was widely shared.
